clue.text: Flower's a boring plant in US soil

indicators.note: in tells us the boring plant and the a sit inside the American soil word

parts.note: mold is the American spelling of mould, rich crumbly soil
a rig is the plant used for boring, a drilling installation

explanation.surface: A gardener notes that a flower sits like a drill in American earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' suggests dullness, but here it means drilling: a drilling RIG.
explanation.definitionFit: The marigold is a common garden plant with orange or yellow blooms, so it is an example of a flower.

indicators.note: in, placed at the end, says the left letter goes inside the centre word

parts.note: mid means centre, as in midpoint

explanation.surface: Someone notes that the soft middle of something has been left inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Mild and soft are synonyms for something gentle or not harsh, as with a mild soap or soft words.

parts.note: litter here is a brood of young animals, and the little bit is its smallest, weakest member

explanation.surface: A scrap of rubbish dropped in the street.
explanation.definitionFit: The smallest and weakest animal born in a brood is called by this name, the undersized one of the bunch.

clue.text: Nepalese express surprise at King Mat turning up

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the whole string of pieces is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: ah is an exclamation of surprise
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
a rug is a small mat for the floor

explanation.surface: A Nepalese person is startled to see a monarch's floor covering flipped over.
explanation.walkthrough: One indicator, 'turning up', turns the whole run AH K RUG, giving GURKHA.
explanation.definitionFit: Gurkhas are soldiers from Nepal serving in British and Indian armies, so the word names a Nepalese person.

parts.note: livery is an informal British adjective for irritable or bad-tempered, as if suffering from a bad liver
a company is a business firm

explanation.surface: A grumpy business in the London financial district.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is the City of London, where the old trade guilds called livery companies still meet; the question mark flags the joke that 'livery' can mean grumpy.
explanation.definitionFit: A livery company is one of the ancient trade guilds of the City of London, so a firm of sorts in the City.

definitions.meaning: in single file, one behind another, as riders on a two-seater bicycle sit
a pair of horses harnessed one in front of the other forms a team of this kind

explanation.definitionFit: Tandem describes things arranged one behind another, and also a two-horse team driven in that line.

clue.text: Food for Rambo is a problem

indicators.note: a problem is something knotty, so these letters are put into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An action hero finds the catering hard to deal with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'problem' rearranges the action hero's name plus IS into AMBROSI, and the final A is kept beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambrosia is the food of the Greek gods, granting immortality, and loosely any delicious food.

parts.note: serving reads as a naval career, but means putting a ball or ring into play, in a game played on board ship

explanation.surface: A description of life in the navy.
explanation.definitionFit: Deck tennis is a game played on a ship's deck, tossing a ring over a net, so serving happens at sea.

parts.note: the Stones suggests the rock band and its fans, but read literally it is someone keen on rocks and minerals

explanation.surface: A Rolling Stones supporter.
explanation.definitionFit: A mineralist is a person versed in minerals, a collector or student of stones, and so a fan of them.

parts.note: both sides are left and right, written L and R
over can mean too, as in overcautious, too cautious

explanation.surface: A car is said to be fitted on its left and right as well.
explanation.walkthrough: L AND R spells out 'both sides' letter by letter, with the AND kept.
explanation.definitionFit: The Land Rover is a British four-wheel-drive off-road car, an example of a vehicle.

parts.note: fare suggests the price of a ticket, but here it is food served on a train, from the carriage where meals are eaten

explanation.surface: A sign at a station telling you the cost of travel.
explanation.definitionFit: A restaurant car is the dining carriage of a train, where meals, the fare, are served.

indicators.note: pointless says a compass point, E for east, is removed

parts.note: a beacon is a signal fire lit as a warning

explanation.surface: A caution about food that seems to have no purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pointless' removes E (east, a compass point) from BEACON.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacon is cured pork from the back or sides of a pig, a staple breakfast food.

clue.text: Sort of short phrase about love's marksman

indicators.note: about says the rearranged letters go around the love letter
to sort is to arrange, so these letters are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
love is nil in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A brief saying about love describes an expert shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of' rearranges the two words into SHARPSHOTER, and 'about' sets that round the love letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharpshooter is a skilled shot with a gun, the same as a marksman.

clue.text: Firm friend on the same team

parts.note: stable means firm, steady
mate is British informal for a friend

explanation.surface: A loyal friend who plays for your side.
explanation.definitionFit: A stablemate is a horse from the same stable, and by extension a colleague, one who is on the same team.

clue.text: One thousand count in extra plant

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

indicators.note: in says the count word sits inside the extra word

parts.note: more means extra, additional
to tell is to count, as a bank teller counts money

explanation.surface: A gardener counts a thousand of some spare plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Immortelle is an everlasting flower whose blooms keep their colour when dried, a kind of plant.

indicators.note: turning means the pieces before it are read backwards as one run

parts.note: PM is the abbreviation for Prime Minister, the premier
taken as written

explanation.surface: A prime minister turning to the press.
explanation.walkthrough: One indicator, 'turning', reads the whole two-piece run backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To tamp is to press or pack down firmly, as with tobacco in a pipe.

clue.text: Incidental call for a late start

parts.note: an occasion is a call or need, as in no occasion to worry

indicators.note: start means the first letter of the word late is taken

explanation.surface: An offhand request for someone to begin later.
explanation.definitionFit: Occasional and incidental both describe something happening now and then, casually or on the side.

clue.text: Fertile, about to act and charming

indicators.note: about says the fertile word goes around the act word

parts.note: arable land is fertile, suitable for crops
to do is to act or perform

explanation.surface: Something fertile and ready to perform is also delightful.
explanation.definitionFit: Adorable and charming are synonyms for something lovable and delightful.

parts.note: toasted suggests raising a glass, but the queen nicknamed this way had the Protestant bishop Hugh Latimer burnt at the stake

explanation.surface: A cocktail raised to honour someone named Latimer.
explanation.walkthrough: Mary I of England burnt Bishop Latimer in 1555, earning a gory nickname that is also a vodka and tomato juice cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bloody Mary is a cocktail of vodka and tomato juice, named after the queen who burned Protestants.

definitions.meaning: a young unmarried woman, the title used for her
a failure to hit or reach, as in a near thing

explanation.definitionFit: Miss is a title for a young woman, and a miss is also a failure to hit the target.

explanation.definitionFit: Entertaining and engaging both describe something that holds the attention pleasantly.

parts.note: mug is slang for face

explanation.surface: A person whose face starts out sad turns out to be self-satisfied.
explanation.definitionFit: Smug and complacent are synonyms for being pleased with oneself.

parts.note: bent on suggests being determined, and a bob a haircut or coin, but a bob is a curtsy, when one leg joint flexes

explanation.surface: Determined to get a short haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: When one bobs a curtsy the knee is the joint that bends.

explanation.surface: Someone spins an excuse for a day off on the spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad-lib describes something spoken without preparation, made up on the spot, which is improvised.

indicators.note: duff is British slang for bad or faulty, so the letters are spoiled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sea song titled after the Shakespearean Scottish thane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'MacDuff' looks like Macbeth's foe, the Scottish thane, but splits in two: its tail 'Duff' is the anagram signal, its head is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A yachtsman is someone who sails a yacht, a sailor.

indicators.note: holds says the still word contains the French article

parts.note: even means still, as in even more
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Stillness grips the French squad.
explanation.definitionFit: A football or cricket side has this many players, so the number stands for a team.

clue.text: Quiet villain has look-in as a preliminary

lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: A quiet crook gets a chance to join in first.
